visual_brief.subject: Claude Cowork moves new Pro and Max tasks to Anthropic's cloud
verified_context: New tasks now execute in Anthropic's cloud, and the previous Only on your computer option is being removed for those plans.
Anthropic says each cloud session receives its own temporary sandbox.
When a task needs a connected folder, browser, local connector, or computer-use capability, the cloud session reaches it through the Claude Desktop app.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: A familiar agent workflow now crosses a new execution and data trust boundary.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A local chamber keeps most files behind its wall while a single file-like slab passes through a narrow guarded bridge into a separate temporary execution chamber.

candidate_notes.A: Rejected at the constitutional gate: the remote chamber contained a robotic arm, which the visual constitution prohibits. It was not scored.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant alternate. The isolated amber chamber and single-file transfer communicate the split runtime, but the dark space setting and floating-rock motif fit the production archive less closely and its native crop was taller than the required wide article placement.
candidate_notes.C: Selected. Separate blue and amber chambers make the changed execution boundary immediately legible; most file-like slabs remain local while one passes through a narrow brokered gateway. The warm paper field, architectural masses, restrained palette, material depth, and centered bridge align with the golden production references and survive wide and thumbnail crops.

crop_review.article_desktop: 1600 x 900 center-cover review: both isolated chambers, the brokered gateway, and the single transferred slab remain fully legible.
crop_review.article_mobile: 359 x 193 center-cover review: the blue local store, amber remote chamber, and connecting slab retain a clear three-part silhouette.
crop_review.thumbnail: 320 x 164 review: the contrasting chambers and narrow transfer path remain distinct without relying on fine detail.

golden_reference_comparison: Compared directly with the repository's OpenAI DNS sandbox and MCP secrets production WebPs. Candidate C shares their warm paper ground, charcoal architectural massing, restrained terracotta emphasis, physical editorial metaphor, and strong foreground/background hierarchy. It is denser and more saturated than the especially airy DNS reference, so Golden Reference Fit is 88 rather than near-identical.
